title: Fourier truncation recovers the function
statement: Let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, and let $k$ be a natural number. If the largest size of a set with a nonzero Fourier coefficient of $f$ is at most $k$, then truncating its Fourier expansion to sets of size at most $k$ gives $f$ itself.
hypotheses_covered: A real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
The Fourier degree of $f$ is at most $k$
